title: The Castle and the Spring
lines: Two fairy maidens were always arguing over which of the two was more beautiful.
They were both so alike and so beautiful
that no one could ever choose between them.
"Well then," said one fairy to the other, "let us settle it another way.
Let us see which of us can make the more beautiful work!
She will be the more beautiful one, too."
One fairy built a wonderful castle on a mountain called Tartod.
It shone and sparkled with gold, silver and diamonds.
It had nine hundred windows, and it turned round and round on its heel.
And what did the other fairy do?
She made a spring burst out at the foot of the mountain.
A spring with healing power.
When both had finished their work, an old traveller came by.
They asked him to be the judge and decide which work was more beautiful.
"It is my castle, isn't it?"
asked the fairy who built the castle.
But the traveller, who was very thirsty, drank from the spring instead of answering,
and at once his thirst was gone, and he felt so well, as if he had grown young again.
"This spring is the more beautiful," he said then, when he saw that
the castle fairy wanted more than a silent answer, "it is finer because it is better."
The castle fairy grew angry, terribly angry.
In her great rage she turned to the mountain and said:
"Well, mountain, I made you beautiful,
but you shall keep your beauty no longer." (Since then the mountain is called Tartod,
which is one of the high mountains of the Szekely Land.)
Then she pulled out the cornerstones of the castle, and of the gleaming,
shining castle not a trace was left; it vanished from the face of the earth.
